multi_instrument_consensus_note: Phase-4 rule (Rossi+2026 procedure): do NOT pick a favourite Ep. The time-integrated Ep estimates are GBM catalog Band 178.9 -36.5/+45.6, GBM catalog Comptonized 983 +/- 183, GBM catalog SBPL break 56.3 -11.5/+15.3, GCN-18404 Band 227 +/- 53, Konus Band 223 -132/+514, Rao+2016 GBM Band 218 +126/-78 and GBM+CZTI 189 +87/-67, BAT+CZTI 160 +215/-67, Chattopadhyay+2019 (0-37 s) 447 +207/-121, Chattopadhyay+2021 (-1.11..30.21 s, GBM+LAT+BAT) 1000 +1008/-139. The spread is NOT measurement scatter: it is driven by (a) whether the fitted band reaches above ~1 MeV and (b) which parametrisation is used - because beta ~ -1.68..-1.75 (> -2) means the nuFnu spectrum RISES above the Band break, so 'Ep' from a GBM-only Band fit is a low break, not the peak. Propagate this as a SYSTEMATIC and quote a per-frame value, never a single number.
redshift: none - no optical/NIR afterglow was ever detected despite 8 campaigns (Kanata T+73 s, MITSuME T+93 s, UVOT T+36 s, OSN, Mondy R>22.4 at 0.31 d, MITSuME Akeno, MITSuME Ks). Dark burst: intrinsic NH = (4.3-5.1)e21 cm-2 at 7.1 sigma (GCN 18407) plus Galactic E(B-V)=0.24. No circular in the 19-circular file contains 'z ='. => NO rest-frame quantity is computable for this burst.

finding: RICH-LITERATURE BURST, and the richest of the doc-layer wave so far: 19 GCN circulars from 8 instruments (Swift BAT/XRT/UVOT, Fermi GBM+LAT/LLE, Konus-Wind, AstroSat CZTI, CALET CGBM, plus 6 optical facilities) and 9 papers carrying burst-specific numbers, of which TWO are dedicated analyses - both co-authored by this project's PI (V. Chand). The burst is historically notable as the first GRB detected by AstroSat CZTI and the first detected by CALET CGBM. The scientifically load-bearing fact for our pipeline is that every wide-band time-integrated fit returns beta ~ -1.7 (harder than -2), so no nuFnu peak sits inside the GBM band; Konus needs Ep = 2600 keV near the peak and our archival LLE-joint fits put Ep at 2-5 MeV. NO published analysis of this burst has ever fitted a double-smoothly-broken power law, while our archival census prefers DSBPL by both AIC and BIC in the time-integrated block and in blk1 - so the two-break test is genuinely NEW work here, not a reproduction.
